task.title: Calibrate booboo static analysis inputs
task.summary: Cancel accidental non-atomic aggregate created during roadmap planning; replace with atomic sprint tasks.

goal.outcome: booboo dead-code and production-readiness findings are calibrated to CodeWiki package entrypoints and dynamic runtime loading.
acceptance: Static analysis config or package metadata declares the real entrypoints: Pi extension, public API facade, scripts, tests, and dynamically imported gateway code.
Dynamic dependency usage such as cytoscape asset loading and scripts/codewiki-gateway.mjs is either visible to the tool or intentionally ignored with a documented reason.
Rerun evidence shows the dead-code list no longer flags known package/runtime entrypoints as unused.
No package behavior or Pi extension loading semantics change except documented metadata/configuration.
User- or config-controlled regular expressions are escaped, bounded, validated, or renamed to explicit regex APIs with invalid-pattern handling.
Glob-to-regex helpers remain covered by tests for *, **, exact path, prefix, and invalid/special-character cases.
Empty catch blocks in roadmap checkpoint and graph rebuild paths are replaced with useful fallback logging, structured warning evidence, or deliberate documented suppression.
Existing gateway, audit, graph rebuild, diagram parsing, and UI smoke behavior remains compatible.
package.json has accurate author/metadata additions that do not break package smoke tests.
CHANGELOG.md exists with an initial entry for current package history or an explicit unreleased baseline.
README or package docs explain Pi extension loading and any intentional absence/presence of npm exports/main/module.
Production-readiness review no longer reports stale or misleading metadata gaps, or remaining gaps are documented as intentional.
A shared module owns resolveImplementationTask, resumeCandidates, task artifact scopes, and shared blocking-status formatting as appropriate.
The command adapter and resume-context tool import shared logic instead of carrying duplicate functions.
Tests cover explicit task selection, session focus, persisted focus, roadmap order fallback, artifact conflict skip, and non-executable task skip.
Existing resume prompt, artifact-status, and status-dock behavior remains compatible.
Duplicate adapter registration blocks are replaced with small data-driven helpers where this improves clarity.
Schema/type duplicate blocks are consolidated only when names and validation semantics remain explicit.
UI theme duplicate helpers are shared or intentionally left duplicated with a short rationale when readability wins.
jscpd duplicate percentage decreases or remaining duplicates are documented as acceptable declaration symmetry.
Major JSON and graph input reads parse as unknown and narrow through local guards or existing domain types.
High-count as any casts in state/builders and state/reader are removed or replaced with narrower typed helpers.
Generated graph/status/task context snapshots remain schema-compatible with existing tests.
Type coverage for state graph/read model files improves measurably in the next review.
Control-room model builders expose typed structures instead of any-heavy object assembly.
Pi UI manager helper inputs/outputs are typed enough to remove easy as any casts.
Adapter tool registration casts are narrowed or centralized behind typed helper functions.
Type coverage for UI/adapter hotspots improves measurably in the next review.
Graph input collection, graph node/edge construction, reconciliation/scope view construction, and file writing are separated into focused modules or helpers.
Existing public imports continue through stable state/API facades where needed.
Generated graph output is byte-stable or differences are explained and covered by tests.
Complexity review shows lower cognitive load for src/state/graph.ts or equivalent split modules.
Roadmap lane/resume/session-state builders are extracted from generic state/builders catch-all code.
Lint category construction and issue creation have focused ownership with typed helper boundaries.
Existing generated status/roadmap/lint outputs remain compatible with smoke tests.
Complexity review shows lower cognitive complexity for state/builders and state/lint owner files.
Roadmap task mutation, sprint mutation, archive/checkpoint handling, and verifier prompt logic have focused module boundaries.
Artifact-status scope normalization, conflict detection, wait queue handling, and mutation persistence have focused module boundaries.
codewiki_task, codewiki_session, and codewiki_artifact_status tool results remain schema-compatible.
Claim/wait queue and roadmap boundary tests continue to pass.
Pi UI manager responsibilities are split into focused modules or helpers for status dock, config panel, roadmap/detail panes, channel editor, and architecture/graph readers.
Web control-room model building is separated from HTTP serving/assets and HTML/JS rendering concerns.
The existing Alt+W/status dock, /wiki-ui, control-room graph asset, and smoke behavior remain compatible.
Complexity review shows reduced nesting/cognitive load in the UI owner files.
Audit profile normalization, file-structure checks, alignment checks, package checks, changed-file checks, and fingerprinting are separated enough to lower fan-out.
Validation preflight, report persistence, verdict handling, and gateway policy checks have clear module boundaries.
Existing audit/validation smoke tests and source-root guard tests remain compatible.
Complexity review shows lower cognitive complexity in audit/tool and validation/report owner files.
